Pigtronix Limited Warranty Page: 5 Contact Information Page: 7 Overview The Pigtronix Disnortion Micro is an analog Fuzz and Overdrive pedal designed to deliver a wide range of saturated tones for guitarists. This compact pedal combines two distinct gain circuits—Fuzz and Overdrive—which can be used simultaneously and routed in either series or parallel configurations, offering significant tonal versatility. At its core, the Disnortion Micro provides a gushing, rich tone that can range from subtle grit to extreme saturation. A single "GAIN" knob controls the saturation level for both the Fuzz and Overdrive circuits simultaneously. This integrated control simplifies the process of dialing in the desired amount of distortion, ensuring that both effects are harmoniously blended. One of the key features of the Disnortion Micro is its routing flexibility, allowing users to switch between "SERIES / PARALLEL" modes. In "Parallel" routing mode, the pedal is ideal for players who want to achieve high gain levels without sacrificing clarity, dynamic response, punch, or low-end presence. This mode effectively "double-tracks" the guitar signal within a single pedal, creating a thick, full sound that retains articulation even with heavy distortion. This can be particularly useful for maintaining note definition in complex chords or fast lead lines while still benefiting from significant saturation. The "Series" routing mode offers an even wider range of gain and more extreme filter effects. In this configuration, the 6-stage CMOS overdrive circuit is cascaded into a unique diode-clipping fuzz, and the combined signal is then output through a 6-way passive filter network. This mode is designed for heavier tones, including metal, and can produce self-oscillating timbres. These unique sounds can be further modulated by the guitar's pickup selection and control settings, allowing for experimental and expressive sonic textures. The ability to generate self-oscillation opens up possibilities for creating sustained drones, feedback-like effects, and other unconventional sounds, making the pedal a tool for sound design as much as for traditional distortion. The pedal's controls are straightforward yet powerful. In addition to the "GAIN" knob, there is a "VOLUME" knob that sets the overall output level of the pedal. This allows users to balance the distorted signal with their clean tone or other effects in their signal chain, ensuring that the pedal doesn't cause unwanted volume jumps or drops. The "DRIVE TONE" knob is specifically for the Overdrive circuit. It sets the cutoff frequency for a low-pass filter on the output of the Overdrive. This control enables users to shape the high-end content of the overdrive, allowing for warmer, darker tones or brighter, more cutting sounds, depending on the desired character. Adjusting this knob can help the overdrive sit better in a mix or provide a distinct voice for different musical contexts. For the Fuzz circuit, the "FUZZ SHAPE" knob is a multi-position switch that selects between 6 different analog filters on the output of the Fuzz. sources.bodyExcerpt: Quick Hit: Pigtronix Octava Micro Review — A Compact Analog Octave Pedal with Surprising Depth | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / gear reviews gear reviews Quick Hit: Pigtronix Octava Micro Review — A Compact Analog Octave Pedal with Surprising Depth By Zoe Langford July 25, 2026 What Is the Pigtronix Octava Micro? The Pigtronix Octava Micro is a true-analog, single-knob octave-down pedal released in early 2023 as a streamlined successor to the full-sized Octava. Measuring just 2.5 inches deep × 4.75 inches wide × 1.75 inches tall and weighing 385 grams, it’s engineered for tight pedalboards without sacrificing core functionality. Unlike digital pitch shifters or DSP-based octavers, the Octava Micro relies entirely on analog circuitry — specifically discrete transistor-based octave synthesis — to generate its sub-octave tone. It accepts standard 9V DC center-negative power (100mA minimum), features true-bypass switching via a soft-touch footswitch, and ships with a custom Pigtronix 9V adapter. At $299 MSRP, it sits between the $199 Boss OC-5 and the $349 EHX POG2 in price — but occupies a unique niche by offering zero-latency analog tracking with no digital conversion artifacts. Analog Tracking Performance: How Fast and Clean Is It? Tracking speed is the make-or-break metric for any analog octave pedal. We tested the Octava Micro using a Fender American Professional II Stratocaster (with Custom Shop '69 pickups), a Gibson Les Paul Standard ’50s (Burstbucker 3 neck, Burstbucker 2 bridge), and a Fender American Elite Jazz Bass — all connected via Mogami Gold Series cables into a Universal Audio Apollo Twin MkII interface running at 44.1kHz/24-bit. Using REW (Room EQ Wizard) and a calibrated Earthworks M30 microphone, we measured signal latency from string pluck to octave output onset: 1.8ms ± 0.3ms across all three instruments. That’s 3.2x faster than the Boss OC-5 (5.7ms average) and 2.1x faster than the POG2 in its fastest analog mode (3.8ms). Real-World Note Accuracy Testing We ran chromatic scale tests across three registers: low E (82.4 Hz), open G (196.0 Hz), and high B (493.9 Hz). The Octava Micro tracked every note cleanly up to 150 BPM in sixteenth-note patterns — a threshold where the OC-5 began misfiring on 3rd-string G (196 Hz) and the POG2 introduced phase-cancellation flutter above 135 BPM. Notably, the Octava Micro maintained stable sub-octave generation down to 65 Hz (low E string fretted at 3rd position), whereas the OC-5 dropped out below 72 Hz and the POG2 exhibited harmonic bleed starting at 69 Hz. Dynamic response was equally impressive. With the Stratocaster’s neck pickup at full volume (7.2V output per DMM measurement), clean picking yielded a rich, warm -12dB sub-octave signal with minimal harmonic distortion ( 7.5V input and introduced 2.3% THD+N under identical conditions. Signal Path & Circuit Architecture Pigtronix doesn’t publish full schematics, but teardown analysis confirms the Octava Micro uses a discrete Class-A transistor ladder filter paired with a precision zero-crossing detector and matched JFET gain stages. There are no op-amps in the critical octave path — a deliberate choice to avoid slew-rate limiting that plagues many hybrid designs. Power regulation is handled by a TPS7A4700 ultra-low-noise LDO delivering ±0.005V ripple at 9V, ensuring stable biasing for the octave generator transistors. Input impedance measures 1.2MΩ (within 2% tolerance across units), while output impedance is 1.8kΩ — compatible with both passive and active pickups without loading issues. True-Bypass Switching Verified We confirmed true bypass using a Fluke 87V multimeter and oscilloscope: with the pedal off, insertion loss was -0.03dB at 1 kHz, +0.01dB at 100 Hz, and -0.07dB at 10 kHz — well within ±0.1dB spec. sources.bodyExcerpt: Pigtronix Philosopher's Tone 2 Optical Compressor Overdrive - Pedal of the Day Reviews Demos Buy a Pedalboard Interviews Contact Navigation Menu Menu Pigtronix Philosopher’s Tone 2 Optical Compressor & Overdrive Posted By Pedal of the Day on Tuesday, July 2, 2024 in Compression / Sustain, Overdrive / Distortion, Pigtronix, Vintage King | 0 comments --> --> After a bit of a break, I’m excited to have another wonderful creation from Pigtronix back for you all today! Compressed overdrive is a sound you can get from your amp, or from pedals, with many variations in tone depending on what order those pedals are in. The Philosopher’s Tone 2 is a compression sustainer with optional grit, kicking it into high gear when you need it the most. Building on the original design, this one has some new tricks up its sleeves… Grab a Philosopher’s Tone 2 from Sweetwater – https://sweetwater.sjv.io/Qy7AEz Elevating the groundbreaking optical compression of the original Philosopher’s Tone to a new plane of tonal enlightenment, the Philosopher’s Tone 2 is a world-class compressor/sustainer with footswitchable Grit, allowing for more versatility than ever before. Featuring a refined implementation of the overdrive circuit first heard in the limited-edition Gold version of this iconic compressor pedal , the unique germanium distortion found in the Philosopher’s Tone 2 delivers smooth top end and rich midrange response, tailored to perfectly match the characteristics of the optical sustainer driving it. A Treble control located just before the master Volume provides 6db of cut or boost at 2kHz for fine-tuning the frequency response of the effect. In addition to Volume and Sustain controls, the Philosopher’s Tone 2 features a parallel clean Blend knob that allows musicians to mix their instrument’s original tone with the compressor/sustainer effect when the Grit circuit is bypassed. This mixing technique restores natural pick-attack and allows clean settings with extreme sustain to remain dynamic and musical. When the Grit circuit is engaged, the Blend knob is automatically bypassed, circumventing the compromises of the original unit and imparting a colorful distortion to your sound in both Germanium and Silicon modes. This nonlinear diode-clipping can range from subtle overdrive to overflowing distortion, all without unwanted feedback. The Philosopher’s Tone 2 also features true-bypass switching and internal 18V power rails for maximum clean headroom that is ideal for use with hot pickups, active bass, synthesizers and other line-level sources. I’ve always love the combination of these two effects genres, and this beauty from Pigtronix really provides a wide range from which to explore and create. Thanks so much to our friends at Sweetwater Sound , as always, for sending this one over for us to check out. There’s more info over on the Pigtronix website as well – check that all out right after you watch our demo video below…cheers!! Introduction: Congratulations on your purchase of the Radial Tonebone Tonebone pedals bring forth a level of quality and performance never before realized in a tube distortion pedal. Whether set for tones commonly described as 'edge', 'crunch', 'metal' or just plain 'scream' the Tonebone gives you rich harmonics and deep bass throughout a wide range of sounds. This manual has been designed to show the user how to gain access to those sounds and more. Once you have read through, take time to experiment. Unpacking your Tonebone: Your Radial Tonebone pedal has been thoroughly tested at the factory, and comes with a 15VDC power supply and this owners manual. We recommend that you keep the box and original receipt in the unlikely event that you should need to send the unit back for servicing. 3. Powering up and getting connected: Before you start, turn your guitar amp volume down to zero. Tonebone comes equipped with a special 15VAC power adapter with enough power to drive the 12AX7 tube inside. When the power suppy is connected, the Tonebone will be in standby mode. Like all tube amps, for best tone let your Tonebone warm up for 5 minutes so that it achieves electrical and thermal stability. The LED on the unit lights up when the foot switch is depressed to indicate it is powered up and ready for use. 4. Using Tonebone The starting point: Start with all the controls at 12 oclock and switches set to the off or at position. Turn your amp up to a comfortable listening level and adjust the LEVEL output control for unity gain, i.e.: the level with Tonebone on (LED is on) matches the level with it off (LED off). Take your time and experiment. sources.bodyExcerpt: Guitar FX Layouts: Ramble FX Marvel Drive Guitar FX Layouts Here's a collection of vero (stripboard) and tagboard guitar and bass effect layouts that we have put together covering many classic and popular effects in growing numbers. Many of these have been posted on freestompboxes.org, so check that site out for great discussions on building your own effect pedals. Enjoy the builds and please also visit us on Facebook and Twitter Pages Home Layout Guide Components Build Guide Offboard Faults Kits Forum Site Map NEW Thursday, 10 July 2014 Ramble FX Marvel Drive Request, thanks to PedalBlotter for his hard graft in tracing the circuit. This is a bit of an awkward circuit to try to find a good middle point to do it on two levels (like my Muff layouts) and have an even spread of components on the board, so I've just done it in a long single row. At 25 x 10 it will still easily fit in a 1590B rotated 90 degrees with lots of space at the sides :o) but I've also included a vertical layout for those who would prefer to build it that way. Info about the original: Great for AC/DC, Led Zeppelin, Hendrix and more! From the KRRR-ANG of the high strings to the growl of the low strings, Marvel Drive delivers all of the tone that made the Marshall™ plexi legendary. Topped with a genuine plexi faceplate, the Marvel Drive uses 4 separate JFET gain stages to create the ultimate in touch sensative, dynamic distortion. Each stage contributes to the harmonics and distortion in much the same way each tube does in an amplifier. A well known secret to great tone out of the vintage, 4 input Marshall™ amps is to use a patch cable to connect 2 of the inputs together. When this is done, the HIGH TREBLE and the NORMAL volumes can be blended together for the perfect crunchy combination. ﻿That is what Marvel Drive recreates. Marvel Drive uses 2 JFET gain stages in parallel, one with a bright and throaty scream, and one that brings the thump of a full stack. Ramble FX browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive overdrive browse by enclosure pedal Ramble FX Marvel Drive Published on May 18, 2013 Ramble FX overdrive pedal Information The Marvel Drive is a unique take on the greatest rock n' roll amp of all time, the British plexi. We all know that great tone, the KRRRR-ANG of the high stings, the growl of the low stings. It can be heard in recordings from all of the greats, including Jimi Hendrix, Led Zeppelin, AC/DC, and many, many more. That is the magic that Marvel Drive captures. The first thing you notice about the Marvel Drive is the genuine gold plexi faceplate, just like the amplifiers have. But what really counts is on the inside. Marvel Drive was designed using stacked and cascaded JFETs which respond like tube stages in an amplifier. It is not another design with clipping diodes that never sound realistic, or a pedal loaded with TMB controls and various switches that don't do much of anything. A well known secret to great tone out of the vintage, 4 input plexis is to use a patch cable to connect 2 of the inputs together. When this is done, the HIGH TREBLE and the NORMAL volumes are both active, in parallel, and can be used to blend the channels together for the perfect crunchy combination. That is what Marvel Drive recreates. Marvel Drive uses 2 JFET gain stages in parallel, one with a bright and throaty scream, and one that brings the thump of a full stack. This configuration delivers a powerful way to get the perfect setting with only 3 knobs. No useless TMB knobs, no extra switches. "I love the way those two volumes interact with eachother. More about the Mig Fuzz: The newly redesigned Mig Fuzz is a classic 4 stage cascading amplifier distortion circuit with a mid range tone control featuring three very useful mods. This unit operates on a standard 9volt power supply (not included) Mod one: (1st toggle) First stage clipping bypass. When active the tone sounds a little warmer. Its not a drastic change but a seasoned musician will notice the difference when playing. Mod two: (2nd Toggle) Tone stack toggle greatly changes sound of tone stack and gives the pedal a more classic “Tone Bender” sound. Mod three: (Mix Knob) This is a repeating theme with RML pedals. It provides a mix between the main distortion and a more gentler overdrive signal. This gives you the option to mix in that more solid signal with your fully distorted signal creating a nice pallet of tonal possibilities. If you love the tone of your amp you don’t have to choose between one or the other. This is a highly recommended pedal for recording. Revv Amplification browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive overdrive browse by type simulation amp simulation browse by enclosure pedal Revv Amplification G3 - Purple Channel Overdrive Published on January 4, 2019 Revv Amplification amp simulation overdrive pedal 2024 Anniversary Edition 2024 Anniversary 2024 Anniversary Edition 2024 Anniversary black sparkle black sparkle v2 v2 v2 Canadian edition v2 Canadian edition Information The Revv Amplification G3 Purple Channel Overdrive is an all-analog high-gain distortion and preamp pedal based on the signature Purple Channel of Revv's Generator 120 amplifier series. Designed as an "amp-in-a-box" recreation of the original channel, the G3 delivers razor-tight low end, focused midrange, and clear, articulate high-gain saturation with a stringy attack that preserves note definition even under extreme gain or downtuned playing. Originally introduced in 2018, the G3 established a benchmark for modern high-gain pedals by translating Revv's flagship amplifier tone into a compact, pedalboard-friendly format. The pedal is engineered to function as a preamp platform rather than a conventional distortion box. It can be run in front of a clean amplifier, into an effects loop return or power amp, or integrated with modelers, impulse responses, and hybrid analog-digital rigs. Smart filtering shapes the frequency response to keep lows tight and highs present, avoiding mud or harshness while maintaining mix-ready clarity. The result is a distortion character that remains defined across a wide gain range, from mid-gain crunch to saturated modern metal lead tones. A powerful 3-band EQ provides extensive tone shaping, allowing the G3 to adapt to various guitars, pickup types, and amplification setups. The pedal's three-position Aggression toggle significantly alters saturation, compression, and low-end response. With the switch in the Off position, the tone is comparatively dry and stringy, offering touch-sensitive mid-gain textures. The Blue mode increases saturation and is often considered a balanced high-gain setting. Red mode delivers the highest gain and compression, producing liquid sustain suited for lead work and thick rhythm tones. The original G3 underwent over a year of research and development

sources.bodyExcerpt: Guitar Effects Pedals by Roger Mayer - Axis Fuzz The Axis Fuzz was developed in early 1967 to give an additional series of tone colours for Jimi. This guitar effect is named after it's most famous use on the title track of the album "Axis Bold as Love". It can also be heard extensively on the "Band of Gypsies" and various other post 1968 recordings by Jimi. Since it's reissue it has become a firm favourite by guitarists who demand rich fill range quality fuzz tones with plenty of bottom end but that can also be used on chords and riffs. It cleans us very well from the guitar volume control and retains its large range of tone colours. The guitar does not loose identity and is truly a modern classic used by many leading performers today. Electronically the Axis uses a discrete circuit configuration that is completely unlike the simple and crude Fuzz Face configuration. Both PNP and NPN silicon low noise transistors are used in an unique configuration that is temperature stable, free from radio interference and producing more output level and sustain than the Classic Fuzz. It produces a distinctive rich-biting sound that makes solos extremely noticeable but not thin sounding and weedy like so many popular mass marketed effects. The unit has a high input impedance to keep the guitars character and quality of tone whist providing great sustain. It is definitely best described as fuzz rather than distortion but has the ability to be used on chords as well as solos.
